subject: [PATCH v4 2/2] iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Default queue depths to one page in a kdump kernel

2026-09-02.patch_summary: This patch modifies the default queue depths in a kdump kernel to one page, reducing memory usage by tens of megabytes. The change affects three queues: command, primary, and event queues. In a normal kernel, these queues are sized based on hardware advertisements and allocated at probe time. However, in a kdump capture kernel, which runs from a small crashkernel reservation, this can lead to significant memory waste. By defaulting the queue depths to one page when is_kdump_kernel() returns true, the patch aims to conserve memory without impacting dump throughput. The change does not affect devices used for saving the dump or those that are switched off outright. An explicit cmdq_entries parameter still allows a capture kernel to request a deeper command queue if needed.

reviews.author: Nicolin Chen
reviews.summary: Suggested breaking down the queue depth calculation into two small helpers for better readability.

2026-09-06.patch_summary: This patch series modifies the default queue depths for the ARM SMMUv3 driver to one page in a kdump kernel, reducing memory usage and improving performance.
